headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0174 — SMTO can't use a document from this location

html:
SMTO-EXE-0174 — SMTO can't use a document from this location

GUID: 417a3a7c-f561-5fcf-b0ac-1cb9d183cbe3
Slug: office-invalid-path
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • SMTO only works with normal files stored in allowed folders on the computer it's using. This location is a web link, network share, shortcut or folder SMTO isn't allowed to use. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the document is on a website or a network share, download or copy it into a normal folder on the computer running the Gateway. SMTO won't open documents directly from web addresses or shared network locations.
  2. If the path is a shortcut or link, use the real file's folder and name instead. Shortcuts could point somewhere unexpected, so SMTO refuses them.
  3. If the file is on your own device, attach it with Add context and ask SMTO to use the attached file. Attached files are placed where SMTO is allowed to open them.
  4. Ask SMTO again using the new location, inside the folder this conversation works in if you can. SMTO may be limited to that working folder for safety.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens the document from the new location.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file location, to the person who manages SMTO. They can check which folders SMTO is allowed to use; don't turn off safety settings just to reach one file.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • File policy or Office local-path validation rejected the path (office.invalid_path): a URL, UNC or network path, a symlink leaf or special file, a path outside the allowed workspace boundary, or another File failure without a more specific mapping.

What this means

  • File policy or Office local-path validation rejected a URL/network path, unsupported regular-file access or other File failure outside its more specific mappings. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • File policy or Office local-path validation rejected a URL/network path, unsupported regular-file access or other File failure outside its more specific mappings.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect target-local path form, actual File policy and file type/links; a path rejection is not proof that the document content is invalid.

How to fix it

  • Use a regular, target-local file within the current File policy on the selected Gateway. URLs, UNC paths, symlink leaves and special files are rejected; when the workspace path guard (Workspace CWD guard, Settings › Operate › Execution) is on, the file must sit inside the workspace root.
  • Use a regular target-local file within current File policy. URLs, UNC paths, symlink leaves and special files are not supported.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use a regular target-local file within current File policy. URLs, UNC paths, symlink leaves and special files are not supported.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended regular local file is accessible within current File policy.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
